content:
Sam: Nimbus follow-up - they want a minimal compatibility POC to swap VendorX -> Redwood. Must-haves: 6 prompt parity checks, a shim that accepts VendorX payloads with minimal client changes, a billing translation (VendorX 50-token buckets -> per-token), and completed security questionnaire covering CMK + retention. Can we scope this quick?
Ivy: I'm fine owning the parity harness. Need their six canonical prompts + a small sample of logs (anonymized) to run tokenization diffs. Will run deterministic and live-sampling tests.
Ken: I'll build the shim. Goal: accept VendorX fields (body key `input_text`, headers `X-VendorX-Session`, `X-VendorX-Client`) and return VendorX-shaped response. Toggle for `logprobs` in compat mode (default off).
Rohit: Security: they require SOC2, IP allowlist, CMK preferred, audit logs, and retention controls. Also asked whether we can redact PII before logs land in S3. I'll prepare the Q/A.
sam: timeline: Nimbus wants demo Thu. Can we have prototype + short diff report + security answers by Wed EOD?
Ivy: Wed EOD is doable for diffs if logs arrive. Parity caveats: VendorX tokenizer differs and sampling defaults (top-p) differ. We'll run with seed + top_k=1 for deterministic comparisons. Also show a non-deterministic baseline.
Ken: Shim sketch: POST /compat/vendorx/generate Headers: Authorization, X-VendorX-Session: s-99 Body: {"input_text":"...","max_tokens":80} Steps: map input_text->prompt, fetch session s-99 -> populate KV last 3 msgs, call Redwood runtime, then transform to VendorX shape: {choices:[{text, finish_reason}], usage:{prompt_tokens,completion_tokens,total_tokens}}. Provide `?compat=vendorx_v1` flag to enable legacy fields like choices[].logprobs (nullable).
Rohit: On CMK: Dedicated/Private -> supported. Hosted CMK -> possible but requires a dedicated workspace + security approval. I'll note approval timeline and checklist.
sec-bot: Reminder: Hosted CMK triggers security ops review and network isolation requirements. See internal runbook (internal link).
Sam: Billing question: VendorX rounds up to 50-token buckets per request. We need a script to translate their logs to per-token billing and show a cost delta (p50/p95). Who can run it?
Ivy: I have a small converter that tokenizes with our tokenizer and can simulate VendorX buckets by rounding up. Will run it on their sample logs and produce a short CSV and summary slide.
Ken: Edge-case: VendorX sometimes includes choices[].metadata and choices[].logprobs; some clients expect them. We'll synthesize minimal metadata (model_name, model_version) by default. Logprobs behind compatibility toggle and contract. Note perf + privacy tradeoff.
Ivy: Also tokenization alignment hack: shim can pre-tokenize with VendorX tokenizer and pass token ids when allowed, which reduces token-delta but complicates portability. Will document as optional.
Rohit: PII redaction: for Dedicated/Private we can enable pre-ingest redaction (regex + NER). For Hosted we can offer allowlisted redaction rules but document recall limitations.
Ken: Example demo curl for Thu:
```
curl -X POST https://demo.redwood/compat/vendorx \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer demo-token" \
  -H "X-VendorX-Session: s-99" \
  -H "X-VendorX-Client: web-2.1" \
  -d '{"input_text":"Summarize the 3 risks for Q3","max_tokens":60}'
```
Response will include choices[0].text and usage.total_tokens to match their billing UI.
Ivy: Latency note: shim adds ~8-12ms on cache hit to assemble KV; cache miss could add +40ms. We'll surface both numbers in the demo.
Sam: Canary plan: propose 5% traffic cutover with fallback to VendorX for mismatches > threshold. Need a short rollout runbook.
Rohit: On returning logprobs: classify as sensitive model metadata; require contract for hosted, allowed for Dedicated/Private with logging controls. I'll include this in the security doc.
Ken: Action items: 1) Ivy -> parity diffs + billing sim CSV (Wed AM). 2) Ken -> shim prototype repo + demo curl (Tue PM). 3) Rohit -> security Q draft + CMK path + redaction notes (Tue noon). 4) Sam -> assemble demo deck and canary/runbook.
Sam: Drop artifacts here when ready. Nimbus wants minimal client changes; emphasise identical response shape and billing explainability. Ping me when you push links. :thumbsup:
